criteria.name: 1. Samsvar konseptord–formuttrykk (Uttrykk + Hovedhensyn)
criteria.what_to_look_for: This is the main grading criterion in the brief: 'Samsvar mellom det valgte konseptordet og det endelige formuttrykket'. The brief also says 'Tenk først og fremst på hvordan kameraet uttrykker konseptordet. Estetikk og teknikk er sekundært.' Ask the framework's two main questions (Hovedhensyn). First, does the object give the right feeling (estetikk): beautiful, interesting, strange, repellent? Second, does it send the right message (semiotikk): what does it symbolise? Without a caption, would a viewer read pull, collapse, light being swallowed, and order sliding into disorder? Or does it just read as 'a dark, sleek camera'? It should express the idea through form (the Uttrykk aspect, as in 'trist' or 'rask'), not illustrate a black hole like a toy or ornament.

criteria.name: 2. Proporsjoner og holdning (første inntrykk)
criteria.what_to_look_for: This is level 1 of the framework, read by squinting or from a distance. Check how the main volumes ('massingen') relate in size and placement, and whether the form is enhetlig (one whole volume) or sammensatt (built from several). Holdning: does the form have a clear visual direction or movement around a central axis, and is it static or dynamic? Visuell vekt and balanse: where does the mass seem to collect? The framework notes that deliberate visual imbalance ('visuell ubalanse') can create movement or dynamics. Forholdet til bakken: how does the camera 'stand' or rest? For this concept, look for mass that seems pulled toward one centre (the lens or optical axis) rather than spread evenly.

criteria.name: 3. Silhuett og negativt rom
criteria.what_to_look_for: Check the outline from above, the side, the front and the back (projiserte riss). Is it a strong, recognisable silhouette that could work as an icon ('silhuetten som ikon')? Is the complexity deliberately simple or complex? Negativt rom is 'like viktig som selve objektet': look at the spaces between and inside the forms. Here the void is the concept itself, so a deep, readable dark opening or recess should carry the composition, not a flat black disc painted on.

criteria.name: 4. Overganger og overflater (kontinuitet, organisk–geometrisk, spenning)
criteria.what_to_look_for: This is level 2. Are transitions sharp, soft, or a deliberate contrast of the two? Where does the form sit on the organisk–geometrisk axis? Read the reflection lines and highlights. Smooth G2/G3 continuity gives even reflections; any break or edge should look intentional ('brudd brukt bevisst'), not like a modelling artefact. Spenning i flaten: does the curvature tighten or change in a controlled way (static vs dynamic surfaces)? Look for surfaces that flow or tighten toward the centre, and one decisive edge where the flow stops.

criteria.name: 5. Sammenføyninger og materialmøter / delelinjer
criteria.what_to_look_for: Do the part lines flow with the form and support the message? Avoid too many lines meeting at one point, 'rat holes' and other line conflicts. Narrow, even gaps signal precision. Rammer or lister (bezels) can handle the transition at the lens or between materials and create layering. Are fasteners visible or hidden, and is that a choice? In an AI or Tripo image, also check for nonsense seams and broken or inconsistent split lines.

criteria.name: 6. Grafisk oppdeling (valør)
criteria.what_to_look_for: Look at the image in greyscale. How are the dark and light areas spread over the object, and in what proportions? Does the valør bring out form features or hide them? Graphics can be the main design theme ('grafikk som bærende designtema'). For this concept, look for a valør gradient or grouping that pulls the eye toward the darkest point. Remember the final physical model is painted in one colour 'slik at formen er lett å lese'. The core effect must therefore survive as form, with real shadow in a recess, and not depend on paint alone.

criteria.name: 7. CMF – farger, materialer og overflatekvaliteter
criteria.what_to_look_for: Do the colour, material and finish (matte–gloss, texture, pattern, metallic lacquer) support the concept rather than being 'limt på til slutt'? Do they also bring in other senses, such as weight, temperature and tactility? Check whether a light-absorbing matte zone and a reflective zone are used meaningfully. The framework notes that metallic paint brings out the form. The hero shot should show the CMF 'slik det er ment å bli produsert'.

criteria.name: 8. Funksjoner og detaljer + Brukssemantikk (affordance)
criteria.what_to_look_for: Check the brief's required functions: lens at least 30 mm in diameter, a utløser (shutter button) and a USB-C port. They should be integrated aesthetically so they feel like part of the design (radii, materials, finish, placement). Ask the affordance question from the semiotics lecture: is it obvious where to hold the camera and what to press? Is there gruppering av funksjoner? Edges: are avfasinger (chamfers), radier (radii) or mikroavfasinger used on purpose? Merking and mikrografikk should be sparse and controlled. Is the detailing done well 'helt ned til den minste detaljen'?

criteria.name: 9. Beskrivende semantikk, arketype og MAYA
criteria.what_to_look_for: Does the object still read as a handheld camera (Beskrivende: typology or category)? Is it in dialogue with the camera arketype, the iconic expected version of the product? Apply the MAYA principle (Most Advanced, Yet Acceptable): is it new and surprising while still recognisable and usable? Too literal or sculptural fails the 'Acceptable' part. Too conventional fails the concept.

criteria.name: 10. Nivåer av inntrykk / stort til lite + helhetlig gestalt
criteria.what_to_look_for: Check that there is a clear hierarchy: first impression (proportions and silhouette), then second impression, third impression, then detailing. Big gestures should dominate, and details should support them without cluttering. Does it look like one coherent final gestalt with a consistently even finish ('jevn modellfinish')? Is the design quality and execution professional?

framework.concept_reading:
The core image is that a camera is already a dark chamber that swallows light. The lens works as a hendingshorisont (event horizon), so the concept and the product archetype (round dark aperture) share one sign. That makes it easier to meet MAYA. Here is how the course framework would express 'Entropi: det som skjer når lys møter eit svart hol', going from stort til lite:

(1) Proporsjoner og holdning: build the main volume as a dynamic holdning around the optical axis as the central axis. Concentrate visual weight toward the lens. Use deliberate visual imbalance so the mass seems pulled, stretched or spiralled inward. The whole body is 'falling' toward one point rather than sitting neutrally in balance.

(2) Silhuett og negativt rom: from the front, a strong silhouette organised around the void. From the side, a form that stretches or tapers toward the lens (tidal 'spaghettification'). The black hole is the negative space itself: a deep recessed lens well whose real shadow does the work. This matters because the final model is painted in one colour.

(3) Overganger og overflater: entropy can be read as a gradient on the organisk–geometrisk axis. Ordered, stringent geometry with crisp edges at the outer shell (low entropy) gradually breaks down. It can melt into continuous, flowing G2/G3 surfaces drawn into the centre, or fragment toward the edges. Spenning i flaten increases toward the lens so reflection lines bend like gravitational lensing. End the flow with one deliberate break: a single sharp edge that is the horizon.

(4) Sammenføyninger and delelinjer: these can follow orbit or spiral paths toward the lens. A lens ramme or bezel should absorb them, so they don't create the line-convergence conflict the framework warns against.

(5) Grafisk oppdeling (valør): light outer surfaces darken into an absolute dark core, so the valør pulls the eye inward.

(6) CMF: contrast a light-absorbing deep-matte core with a gloss or metallic outer zone that catches and 'bends' light. Texture can grow more disordered toward one end as an entropy cue.

(7) Funksjoner og detaljer: place the utløser (shutter button) along the inward flow, like something about to be swallowed. Hide the USB-C port in a dark or lower-order zone. Grip affordance must stay clear (Brukssemantikk). The course's kiki–bouba reference fits: a bouba-like smooth pull at the centre against kiki-like fragmented edges.

Main risk: a literal illustration (an accretion disc stuck on a box) instead of an expressive form.

Note: the course material never uses Peirce's ikon/indeks/symbol. Its semiotics vocabulary is the four semantiske aspekter (Beskrivende, Uttrykk, Brukssemantikk, Identitet; Sunde/Monö), plus arketype, MAYA and kiki–bouba. The semantiske virkemidler are proporsjoner, grafikk and overflater. The framework's six steps are: Proporsjoner og holdning; Overganger og overflater; Sammenføyninger og materialmøter; Grafisk oppdeling (valør); CMF; Funksjoner og detaljer. Sources: /root/.claude/uploads/b6113a1b-6fee-5055-a29d-0117c791e712/6ff28a72-03_Formanalyse_Rammeverk.pdf, /root/.claude/uploads/b6113a1b-6fee-5055-a29d-0117c791e712/e82a5523-02_Semiotikk.pdf, /root/.claude/uploads/b6113a1b-6fee-5055-a29d-0117c791e712/c6ab11aa-FormNerd_-_Prosjektoversikt.pdf.

candidates.prompt: Turn this sketch into a photorealistic industrial-design studio render of a palm-sized handheld camera, same 3/4 front view, proportions and composition as the sketch. Concept: light meeting a black hole. Core body: matte black, light-absorbing paint. Over it, soft inflated light-grey tubes in satin soft-touch finish: they form a rounded hand grip on the left, run up over the top, twist and cross each other in a loose braid between the two top blocks, and one tube curves down and wraps fully around the lens as a thick continuous torus, a satin light-grey photon ring. The ring is solid painted material: no LED, no glow, no emitted light. Lens: inside the ring the black body funnels inward like a smooth event-horizon cone, and at the bottom sits a real recessed camera lens about 35 mm in diameter: black anodized barrel with fine knurling, dark coated glass front element with subtle concentric reflections of inner elements and a faint purple-green coating sheen. Details: dark rectangular viewfinder block top rear left; dark cylindrical dial block top right with knurled black cap; round black domed shutter button on top of the grip; small USB-C port visible on the left outer side face of the grip in a black inset panel. Crisp continuous surfaces, clean part lines, reads as a 3D-printed and painted design model. One single camera fully in frame, centered, seamless pure white background, large softbox key light from upper left, soft contact shadow, high-end product photography, sharp focus. No text, no logos, no watermark, no glowing ring, no extra objects, no hands.
candidates.self_assessment: This is the closest match yet to the sketch: same 3/4 view, the grip flows into tubes that cross over the top between the viewfinder and dial blocks, and one tube wraps the lens as a satin grey ring with no LED glow. All three requirements are clearly visible: a real knurled lens with concentric purple-green coating reflections, easily over 30 mm against the palm-sized body; a black shutter button on top of the grip; and a USB-C port in a black inset on the left side of the grip. The main weakness is that the concept now reads weaker than the calibration image. The lens sticks out instead of sitting at the bottom of a black funnel, so the black-hole pull is mostly lost. The tubes cross only once, so they show little growing disorder. The grip is one smooth blob rather than separate tubes, and the overall feel is friendly and toy-like rather than about entropy. candidates.prompt: Turn this sketch into a photorealistic industrial-design studio render of a compact handheld camera, same 3/4 front view and proportions as the sketch. Concept: entropy, light falling into a black hole. The form reads left to right as ORDER -> DISORDER -> ABSORPTION. Core body: deep matte black light-absorbing paint. Over it run five soft inflated light-grey tubes in satin soft-touch paint. LEFT, low entropy: on the hand grip the five tubes form a calm, tidy, perfectly parallel bundle of equal thick tubes, evenly spaced, running vertically up the grip. TOP, rising entropy: crossing the top between the dark viewfinder block and the dark dial block, the tubes stretch progressively thinner, fan apart and twist into an irregular braid. RIGHT, absorption: the thin stretched strands curve down onto the front and spiral inward around the lens in tighter and tighter coils, a narrowing vortex visibly pulled into the lens barrel and vanishing inside it. Lens: a real camera lens about 35 mm diameter at the spiral center, black anodized knurled barrel, dark coated front glass with concentric inner reflections and faint purple-green coating sheen. All solid painted material: no LED, no glow, no emitted light. Details: dark viewfinder block top rear; dark dial block top right with knurled cap; round black shutter button on top of the grip, clearly visible; small USB-C port clearly visible on the left outer side of the grip in a black inset. Clean surfaces, reads as a 3D-printed and painted design model. One single camera fully in frame, seamless pure white background, softbox key light from upper left, soft contact shadow, sharp focus. No text, no logos, no glowing ring, no extra objects, no hands.
candidates.self_assessment: The concept reads very clearly from left to right. The grip has a tidy parallel bundle of tubes (order), the tubes braid chaotically over the top (disorder), and on the front they converge and coil tightly around the lens barrel (absorption). All the requirements are clearly visible: a real lens, well over 30 mm, with knurled barrel and coated glass; a black shutter button on top of the grip; and a USB-C port in a black inset on the left side of the grip. The main flaws: the soft, inflated tubes from the sketch became thin cords or cables, and there are more than five of them. They do not visibly thin out as they cross the top. They wrap around the outside of the protruding barrel rather than being swallowed into a void, so the effect reads more like "tied up" than "sucked in". The body has also turned into a conventional boxy mirrorless camera, losing the sketch's soft mass and photon ring. The thin strands hanging free in the air would also be fragile and hard to 3D print and paint. Calls: the first call was rejected by the API before any task was created (code 1004, prompt over 1800 characters), so it cost no credits. The one allowed retry, with a shortened prompt, succeeded and cost 15 credits.

scores.rationale: It has the clearest story without a caption. The white grip turns to grey tube and then to a black core at the lens, so light is visibly swallowed, and the body slumps toward a nested, stepped double ring around the lens. The gradient (colour) does more of that work than the form does, and the rings are soft, static donuts with no decisive horizon edge.

It is the only candidate where the black hole is carried by form. A deep, flaring black funnel sinks the lens back, so real concave shadow would still read after the model is painted one colour. But the funnel reads like a rubber lens hood. Valør is a plain two-tone split, not a progression, and the tube braid on top is unchanged from the sketch, so there is no order-to-disorder narrative.

It has a strong semiotic gesture: a real recessed void, and one tube that dives into the hole and is swallowed, plus a more tangled braid. But the LED ring is exactly the literal accretion-disc gimmick doing the work the form should do. The void-as-lens also breaks the camera sign the concept is meant to share.

It has the most literal entropy read. Ordered parallel cords on the grip unravel into a tangle and spiral tightly around the optical axis. But it is cords applied to a static, conventional box (the 'disc stuck on a box' risk), and the lens protrudes outward instead of reading as an inward void.

The torus's inner face darkens as it rolls into the lens, a hint of light falling over a horizon. That effect is mostly airbrushed valør on a shape identical to A, and it would largely vanish once painted one colour.

Faithful to the sketch, but it reads as a friendly inflated camera with a soft bumper ring around a proud, outward-pointing lens. There is no pull, no void and no progression, so 'entropy' and 'black hole' do not come through.
No image was produced. Only a payload file exists, so there is nothing to judge on concept or form.

judgements.winner_edits:
Edits to f_light_gradient, aimed at moving the meaning from paint into form:
1) Make the void a real form. Sink the lens 15-25 mm into a funnel that tightens as it goes in. The stepped rings should increase in curvature tension toward the axis, so the shadow goes black even with single-colour paint. End the funnel at ONE crisp knife-edge lip (the event horizon), where the soft G2/G3 flow breaks sharply into the recess. Right now every ring is a soft pillow and there is no decisive break.
2) Change the concentric donuts into an inward spiral. Let the grip tube enter the lens ring and coil about 1.5 turns down into the recess, thicker where it enters and thinner as it descends. That way the ring reads as being pulled in rather than as a static bumper. Push the inner ring's radius much tighter than the outer one so the two stop reading as stacked donuts.
3) Add a form gradient along the organic-geometric axis (entropy from order to disorder). Start the grip and the viewfinder and dial blocks as crisp, ordered geometry (tight radii, chamfers, flat planes). Let the shell soften, inflate and flow as it nears the lens. Today the grip is already fully bouba, so the form itself has no order-to-disorder progression.
4) Add spaghettification to the tube. As the grip band crosses the top, it should stretch thinner and faster (higher tension), then compress and coil at the lens. Avoid the uniform thickness or fattening it has now.
5) Use deliberate visual imbalance in the holdning. Lower and lean the top line toward the optical axis. Shear or lean the upright viewfinder block and dial block toward the lens, so the ordered elements are visibly being deformed by the pull rather than standing untouched.
6) Make the CMF follow the form instead of a flat left-to-right fade. Run the light-to-dark gradient along the tube's path. Use a satin or pearl metallic on the grip so reflection lines catch and bend toward the lens (gravitational lensing). Reserve a deep, light-absorbing velvet matte only for the funnel. Check the result as a single-colour greyscale render to confirm the read survives the one-colour painted model.
7) Put the details on the narrative. Tilt the shutter toward the lens and place it where the grip band starts to stretch, so it sits on the inward flow. Move USB-C into the dark, low-order zone under the well. Fix the posterised banding so the gradient reads as a material, not as a filter.

scores.rationale: It keeps the sketch's main gesture: the grip tube runs over the top, the tubes cross between the viewfinder and dial blocks, and the torus wraps the lens. The torus's inner face rolls into a dark throat, so the lens sits in a real recess that would still cast shadow on a model painted in one colour. The lens is credible (well over 30 mm), with the shutter on top of the grip and USB-C on the side of the grip. It loses points for the leather-like micro-wrinkles on the surface and the deep V-crease between the grip block and the front tube, which would be hard to fill, sand and paint.

This is the most faithful to the sketch and the cleanest execution: even matte surfaces, controlled tube sweeps and clean junctions. The grip is clean and easy to hold, with the shutter on top and USB-C in a dark inset panel. It would be easy to print as separate tube and core parts. But the lens ring is a uniform light donut and the lens sits proud of it, so there is no void or depth. At the crit it risks reading as 'a camera with pool noodles' rather than light being swallowed.

The deep matte-black cowl around the lens creates real negative space that will survive single-colour paint, and it shows a viewfinder eyepiece. The body has the same clean grip, shutter and USB-C as a. However, it drops the sketch's key gesture of the light tube wrapping the lens. The right tube ends ambiguously behind the cowl, which reads more like a rubber lens hood or eyecup than an event horizon.

It has the strongest valør idea: white grip to black lens, with stacked dark tori forming a stepped well around a credible knurled lens. It stays close to the sketch. But the surfaces are lumpy with an orange-peel texture, the render shows posterisation and banding artefacts, and the proportions are upright and toy-like. The full white-to-black fade across the tubes would also need careful airbrushing.

It is a credible camera, with a real lens, shutter and USB-C, but it replaces the sketch's fat inflated tubes with about ten thin cords that cross at random. There is no real lens glass, only a black hole with a glowing LED ring, so the 30 mm lens requirement is not credibly met. The LED ring reads as a gimmick. scores.rationale: This is the cleanest input for image-to-model. It shows one matte object fully in frame under soft, even studio light, with a clear torus around a solid, recessed lens and a plausible block structure for the back. The only risks are the over/under tube crossing on top and the dark, low-shading core, where depth may flatten.

It is close to A and also clean, fully framed and evenly lit. Two things make it harder to read than A. The vertical tube lobe on the grip front adds overlap, and the ring's darkening toward the lens looks like painted shading, so Tripo may not read it as real depth. The slight leathery surface texture may also bake in as noise.

Replacing the ring tube with a funnel cuts self-occlusion, and the silhouette is strong. The drawback is that the large, nearly unshaded matte-black funnel and core merge into one dark mass, which makes the depth of the recess ambiguous for reconstruction. The eyepiece on the viewfinder also faces sideways, which is confusing.

The square frame holds a compact, strong silhouette with few thin parts. However, on the right side the ring, tubes and body go dark grey against black, so their edges merge. The image also has visible posterization/banding artefacts that may bake into the texture or add surface noise.

Lighting and framing are good, but there are a dozen-plus thin interwoven cables with air gaps beneath them. That is the worst case for Tripo, which will likely fuse them into a lumpy shell or produce broken, non-manifold strands. The long protruding lens barrel also hides much of the body.

The emissive glow ring is the main feature, and it will bake into the texture as a flat white band with no defined geometry. A tube threads into the black void through-hole, which creates topological ambiguity. The 'lens' is an undefined dark hole rather than a solid, readable surface.

CALLS AND CREDITS. I sent 4 API requests and 2 were billed. The first two attempts (g_hero 2178 characters, g_to3d 1884) were rejected at task creation with error code 1004, "prompt must be at most 1800 characters". No task was created and no credits were spent. As the rule allows after an API error, I shortened each prompt and retried once (1779 and 1627 characters). Both retries succeeded at 15 credits each: task 1c1bb81a-4931-4733-8138-15768cbbba41 for g_hero and task 23510474-1ec4-4947-ad86-6f5ffe1042c6 for g_to3d. That makes 30 credits from this step. The shared balance read 305 before and 245 after, a drop of 60. The other 30 is not from these tasks and is probably other agents using the same account at the same time. Payloads are at /home/user/formnerd/entropi/payloads/g_hero.json and g_to3d.json. Result records are at /home/user/formnerd/entropi/images/g_hero.json and g_to3d.json. g_hero is 2400x1792 (4:3); g_to3d is 2048x2048 (1:1). Both used banana_pro with input = c_gravity_well.

WHAT I ASKED FOR (both prompts). From the judges' notes, I asked for:
- A deep funnel that steepens toward the axis and ends at one crisp knife-edge lip (the event horizon), with the lens glass about 15 mm deep behind it.
- The right front tube to coil about 1.5 turns down into the well, getting thinner as it goes.
- Spaghettification: tubes full at the grip, thin over the top, compressed into the coil.
- Tubes fused at the crossing with no air gaps.
- An order-to-disorder gradient: crisp chamfered blocks leaning slightly toward the lens, the shell softening toward the lens.
- The shutter moved forward onto the flow with a thin titanium bezel.
- USB-C kept on the left side of the grip in a recessed black inset. The design notes allow this option, and it keeps the port visible from the 3/4 view.
- A visible eyepiece and one knurled dial cap.
- A 50 mm knurled ring with a 38 mm front element.
- CMF for g_hero: pearl light-grey tubes fading along their path to graphite, a velvet black throat, matte black core, no banding, no LED or glow.
- For g_to3d: dark near-matte glass with no purple or green reflections, filleted contact patches with no floating parts, matte or satin finishes only, 25-30 degree elevation, a long lens, centred with a 10% margin, even light, a rim light on the black surfaces, and only a small contact shadow.

WHAT ACTUALLY CHANGED (honest assessment from side-by-side crops). banana_pro in edit mode held very closely to the input. Both outputs are close re-renders of c_gravity_well, and the big form edits did not come through.
- g_hero: the shutter and the dial cap are now spun brushed titanium. The whole shutter button became metallic rather than getting a thin bezel, and it stayed in the same spot on top of the grip. The tube paint is a slightly cooler, smoother satin grey. Everything else matches the winner. The lens and well are essentially unchanged: a thick soft black bezel, with no crisp lip, no deeper throat and no spiral coil. There is no grey-to-graphite gradient along the tubes, the blocks do not lean, and the tubes still have even thickness. The requirements are still met: a real lens of about 35-38 mm, a visible shutter, a visible USB-C port on the left side of the grip in a black inset, and an eyepiece. There is no glow. The image reads as a clean, premium studio render.
- g_to3d: the view is square and a little more frontal and higher. The object is centred with about 8-10% margin, the light is even and neutral, all surfaces are matte, and the contact shadow is small. The lens coating reflections are toned down, but some purple sheen remains. The shutter and USB-C are simple and visible. The form edits are again missing: the over/under tube crossing and the shallow bezel well are still there, with no spiral. It is usable as a single-view Tripo input. The rear is still not shown or described.

RECOMMENDATION if the orchestrator gets more budget. To get the real form changes (crisp lip, coil, gradient), don't run a single-input banana_pro edit of the winner. Either pass the sketch as input with a fresh full description, or use "inputs" = [winner, d_fusion_refs] and refer to them as image[1] and image[2]. Also keep every prompt under 1800 characters, because that is the hard API limit.
